column7: Sibling of #4520 in the PAT and machine-token network allowlists: EncodePATCIDRs appended /32 to the input text of a bare ::ffff:a.b.c.d, storing the IPv6 network ::/32, so the token was refused from the intended host and accepted from ::1 and every ::/32 address. New entries are stored as the IPv4 network they name; IPInCIDRs (rules.ParseAllowlistCIDR) reads a stored row in exactly the old shape (mapped /32) as the IPv4 host, a narrowing, and skips any other stored mapped prefix below 96 (fail closed, never widened). NAT64 and other dotted-tail IPv6 entries are unchanged. Found by SECURITY-WAVE1-REVIEW
